questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Weather, nature, adventures

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was hard finding which courses was available to take. Other than that, everything was very easy to acces and find

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
There was a car picking us up from the airport helping us to get to our accommondation. There was orientation week where we received all the basic informations.
It took however over two weeks to get the classes, and the staff was super busy, and they didn't have a lot of time to help us with getting the right classes.

Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you chose housing on campus, you can choose between either Academia or Concordia but there are located within the same gated area. You have to apply through their webpage relatively early.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a few options getting meals delivered every day, but I did not try that myself. However, it seemed to be very unhealthy and not worth the money.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The good thing about living on campus is that it's very safe. The houses is gated all hours and security guards are also walking inside the gate at night to control the area. I never felt unsafe there. Also, living at campus you are living with a lot of the other exchange students and it's easy to meet people, especially in the beginning. When you are not from either Academia or Concordia, you cannot easily enter the gated area and this also mean that you will not be able to be a part of all the parties and gaterings in there. There is also a little supermarket in the gated area which is very nice to have. The gated area is located at Bosman street which is 15/20 minuted walking distance from central Stellenbosch which is alright. However, the houses itself is very old, the bed is not very good and just in general the rent is very expensive compared to what you get. The housing off campus is much nicer, the rooms are bigger, and there are also pools and gardens connected to the houses most of the time - and the rent is also cheaper. You will most likely meet more South African students there and not only exchange students that mostly live at Academia or Concordia. If I could redo it, I would have choosing housing off campus but it depends what you prefer.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to fill out a paper regarding your classes and send to the university before arriving. When you arrive, you receive and mail with the classes which you have been accepted into. However, you can change your classes if you decide to take another course after you have arrived.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The staff was very busy during registration. However, you can book a meeting with one of the staff members and they will help you through registration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't get one of the courses I really wanted. But other than that, it went good.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into the course catalog carefully and choose more courses than you need in case some of the get cancelled. You can only choose between those courses you pick in the beginning.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses is well structured and the professors are very good. However, the level is as high as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is lectures and the professor speaks only beside some student presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International tax law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International tax law. Very good and helpful professor. Very well structured and professional.

questions.answer: The visum application is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The supermarket is expensive in South Africa. It's is therefore also sometimes cheaper to eat out rather than cooking at home. Clothes is the same price as in Denmark.
The coffee is very cheap. Uber is very cheap. Renting cars and going on trips is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are all kinds of activities connected to the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I played tennis at the Stellies tennis Club. I also attended the Wine society and ISOS where you go on trips and see South Africa.
I can recommend any sports klub and the Wine Society was very fun as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can recommend going to the west cost national park during spring time, all the wine farms close to Stellies, Capetown (haut bay, camps bay, Cliften beach, Müizenberg to surf), the Garden Route, Drakensbergs Mountain, Panorama route, Krüger national park, Namibia

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would live off campus. Be on the buddy program and get to know your local buddy. Attend any society or sports club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The "african" time - every thing takes a lot of time, people are always late. Also you get to see a lot of property, and a huge gap between the social layers. It's not very safe there, especially when you are a white girl - you cannot walk alone in the dark and you always have to be extra careful.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people take it very easily and it is very chilled.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. chose housing off campus, 2. South Africa has a lot of property and can be unsafe if you do not take your precautions, 3. save a lot of money so you have enough money to travel around the country and experience the most beautiful country in the world.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It can get very cold in Stellenbosch and it also rains a lot during winter/spring and autumn. 

Study is easy so you have lots of time traveling and experience the beautiful country. 

I would recommend renting a car for the entire semester. In the end, it is more expensive taking Ubers wherever you go. Also, having your own car gives you more flexibility. Because it is not safe to walk in the dark, it is very nice to have a car to drive to and from you accommodation.

Regarding safety, I did not feel unsafe during the day when there was sunlight. I walked alone during those hours and was also taking runs around the town. Stellenbosch is in general one of the most safest towns in South Africa and not a lot of crime happens there. But you should always be cautious.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The travels and all the experience I gained and all the people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Seeing property a lot was difficult for me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Living in Stellenbosch reminds me of an old european town. It is such a cute little town surrounded by the mountains and wine farms. If you love wine, you should definitely study at Stellenbosch University.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
